title: Enterprise SDK intake framework for language support, auth patterns, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Problem: We're receiving higher-volume, enterprise-grade requests around SDK language support (Java/Go/.NET), standardized auth patterns (SSO/SAML/OAuth, token-exchange), and improved streaming ergonomics (client backpressure, reconnect/fallthrough). Currently intake is ad hoc: PMs and SEs capture requests in docs and Slack, engineering teams get fragmented asks, and we lack a reproducible prioritization rubric for enterprise vs self-serve work.

Goal: Define a repeatable intake and prioritization framework that triages SDK and client library requests into: self-serve (docs + examples), SDK enhancement (minor surface/API changes), and eng engagements (new language SDK or enterprise SSO integration). The framework should capture security needs, expected usage scale, number of customers requesting, and implementation complexity to produce a clear priority and an SLA for response/commit.

Proposed intake form fields (minimum):
- Customer name / contact / customer tier
- Use case & criticality (e.g., product feature behind SLA)
- Target language/runtime + preferred package manager/version
- Auth pattern required (API key, OAuth2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, token exchange)
- Streaming requirement (server->client, client->server, bidi; expected RPS; latency SLO)
- Data residency / compliance requirements
- Expected rollout size (pilot, team, org-wide)
- Timeline constraint (must-have date)
- Links to any existing customer code or PoC

Prioritization rubric (scoring):
- Business impact (0-5): revenue or strategic customer influence
- Security/compliance complexity (0-5): whether requires security review or KMS/HSM
- Implementation complexity (0-5): new language or new infra patterns vs small API tweak
- Reusability (0-5): applies to multiple customers or core product surface
- Maintenance cost (0-5): ongoing burden (bindings, support surface)
Weighting suggestion: Business impact 30%, Security 25%, Implementation 20%, Reusability 15%, Maintenance 10%.

Triage flow (proposed):
1) Intake submitted (via Confluence template or internal intake form).
2) PM Triage (within 3 business days): verify fields, ask clarifying Qs, initial score.
3) Route:
   - Self-serve: route to Developer Docs + sample apps (target 2-week turnaround).
   - SDK enhancement: small surface changes routed to SDK backlog (estimate <5 pts).
   - Eng engagement: new language or enterprise SSO token exchange -> open cross-functional ticket with ENG/SEC/DES owners.
4) Assign priority and comms cadence; notify customer-facing SE/AE.

Decisions and constraints:
- First-phase languages to target for eng engagement: Java and Go (largest enterprise demand). Later phase: .NET and Ruby if adoption metrics support.
- Streaming ergonomics: adopt a common interface across SDKs: evented streaming callbacks + an async iterator where languages support it. Ensure first-class reconnect/backpressure primitives.
- Auth patterns: implement a canonical token-exchange flow for SSO/SAML where Redwood acts as the verifier but does not persist customer SSO credentials; document an enterprise integration guide and a reference implementation in Java.

Trade-offs considered:
- Building first-class SDKs for many languages increases maintenance burden; prioritizing Java/Go covers most enterprise requests but may frustrate smaller customers requesting niche runtimes.
- A heavyweight enterprise SSO integration increases security review time; consider an MVP reference implementation plus a hardened GA version after a security audit.

Metrics to track post-rollout:
- Number of incoming SDK requests closed as self-serve vs eng engagement
- Time-to-first-response and time-to-commit for enterprise requests
- Adoption (install counts, SDK downloads) in first 90 days
- Support ticket volume related to auth/streaming failures

Next steps (owners):
- Create Confluence intake template and short internal form (PM: Priya — due 2026-03-10) [DONE].
- Run intake with top 10 open enterprise SDK asks and score them (PM: Priya — due 2026-03-12).
- Kickoff cross-functional scoping for top-2 requests (PM+ENG+DES+SEC) (Owner: Priya & Eng leads — kickoff by 2026-03-18).
- Draft PRD for Java SDK streaming + SSO reference (Owner: Jordan — draft by 2026-03-22).

Notes: Links in the comments include PRD draft, design sketches, and a GitHub prototype for streaming helpers. Customer ask backlog includes a Fortune 100 insurance customer requesting Java SSO integration and a fintech startup requesting server-side streaming with client reconnect semantics.
